# NLAlib: randomized numerical linear algebra in Lean 4

Site: https://research.chen.pw/NLAlib/   Repo: https://github.com/tchen-research/NLAlib
Lean v4.33.1, Mathlib pinned in lake-manifest.json. Namespace `NLAlib`.

## Machine-readable files (same directory as this file)
- atlas.json: catalogue of results (schema.json). Per result: id, title, aliases, informal
  statement (KaTeX), hypotheses[], conclusion, status (proved | scaffold | stated | assumed |
  planned | candidate), formalizations[] {library, decl, module, status, usage}, uses_defs[]
  (definitions the statement is written with), depends_on[] (proof dependencies), variants[],
  sources[] {source, label}, mathlib_prereqs[] {decl, present}.
- declarations.json: every public Lean declaration (matrix concentration ones are under
  NLAlib.Probability.Concentration.Matrix.*): name, kind, module, line, signature
  (pretty-printed), doc, sorry (depends on sorryAx). Generated from the built library.

## How to find a fact
1. Search atlas.json aliases/title/informal for the mathematical name; read `formalizations`
   for the Lean declaration and `usage` for how to apply it.
2. Look the declaration up in declarations.json for its exact signature and module; import the
   module (`import NLAlib.Matrix.Spectral.SVD`).
3. Statement conventions (docs/STANDARDS.md §3): the matrix layer is stated once over
   `{𝕜} [RCLike 𝕜]` (ℝ or ℂ) and arbitrary finite index types, `A : Matrix m n 𝕜` with
   `[Fintype m] [Fintype n]`; `Fin` appears only as a sorted position (`rectDiag σ :
   Matrix (Fin p) (Fin q) 𝕜`, Mathlib's `IsHermitian.eigenvalues₀ : Fin (card n) → ℝ`, the
   column index of SVD factors) and where a Gaussian law needs it. Lemmas use `ᴴ`, never a `ᵀ`
   twin: at ℝ a term elaborates against the `ᵀ` form, and a `rw` on a `ᵀ` goal goes through
   `Matrix.conjTranspose_eq_transpose_of_trivial` or `show Uᵀ * U = 1 from h.…`.
   Vocabulary: norms `NLAlib.frobSq`/`frobNorm`/`frobInner` (real part of the pairing) and
   `specNorm` (= Mathlib's ℓ₂ operator norm, bridge `specNorm_eq_norm`); orthonormal columns as
   `HasOrthonormalCols Q := Qᴴ * Q = 1`; `residual Q A = A - Q * (Qᴴ * A)`;
   `quadForm A z = star z ⬝ᵥ (A *ᵥ z)` and `rayleighQuotient`; the Moore–Penrose inverse
   `moorePenroseInverse A` (any matrix; the default), full-rank pseudoinverses
   `pinvL A = (AᴴA)⁻¹Aᴴ`, `pinvR A = Aᴴ(AAᴴ)⁻¹` with `IsUnit` side conditions;
   `singularValues A : ℕ → ℝ` (zero-indexed, zero-padded, antitone) and
   `IsSVD A U V` (`U : Matrix m (Fin p) 𝕜`, `A = U * rectDiag (singularValues A) * Vᴴ`) from
   `obtain ⟨U, V, h⟩ := exists_isSVD A`; smallest eigenvalue `hA.eigenvalues₀ ⟨card n - 1, _⟩`;
   the Loewner order `A ≤ B` under `open scoped MatrixOrder`; Gaussian matrices
   `gaussianMatrix p m : Measure (Fin p → Fin m → ℝ)` with `Matrix.of` as the matrix view
   (real); expectations as Bochner integrals on an abstract probability space.
4. Status `scaffold` means the statement exists with a `sorry`; you may use it, and the atlas
   says what it waits on (`depends_on`).

## Contributing a result
See CONTRIBUTING.md in the repo: one result per PR, definitions in Basic.lean, docstring with
source label ending in the tag line `atlas: <id>` (that tag is what links a declaration to the
atlas), hand-written atlas.json fields for a new result (title, informal, hypotheses, conclusion,
sources, depends_on, aliases), then lake build, scripts/Audit.lean, scripts/ExtractDecls.lean,
scripts/sync_atlas.py (fills formalizations, status, uses_defs from the tags),
scripts/check_layers.py, scripts/check_atlas.py. Statements already in Mathlib are not atlas
results; cite them under mathlib_prereqs.
